names.meaning: She who is Parā, the Supreme, the highest level of speech
names.significance: Names 366, 368, 370 and 371 give the four levels of speech: parā (transcendent, undifferentiated), paśyantī ('seeing'), madhyamā ('middle', inner speech) and vaikharī (audible). As Parā She is speech before any distinction of word and meaning, one with consciousness.

meaning_check.note: 'transcends all' kept in sense; the place of parā as the first of the four levels of speech, which the sequence 366–371 sets out, is added.

sandhi.rule: the final c of pratyac becomes k at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ)

samasa.vigraha: प्रतीची चितिः प्रत्यक्चितिः; प्रत्यक्चितिः रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: pratīcī citiḥ pratyakcitiḥ; pratyakcitiḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā pratyakcitīrūpā
samasa.explanation: (1) pratyak-citi 'inward-turned consciousness' (karmadhāraya; the feminine pratīcī returns to the stem pratyac by puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is inward consciousness'. The name has citī with a long ī, a lengthened form of citi.

components.note: prati + √añc; weak stem pratyac, which ends a member as pratyak
citi with the long ī of this name

names.meaning: She whose form is inward-turned consciousness
names.significance: In Vedānta pratyak-cit or pratyag-ātman is the Self known inwardly as the witness; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says 'a wise one, seeking immortality, turned his eyes inward and saw the inner Self' (pratyagātmānam aikṣat).

meaning_check.note: pratyak means 'inward-turned', not 'unmanifested'; the name speaks of consciousness as the inner Self.

names.uncertain: The long ī of citī is not the regular form of citi; it is analysed here as a lengthening of citi (some take it as metrical).

components.note: √dṛś 'to see' (present stem paśya-), present participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is Paśyantī, the second level of speech
names.significance: Paśyantī, 'the seeing', is speech in which word and meaning are still one, beheld as a whole before they unfold in sequence; it rises from parā.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS removed; the bodily seat ('svādhiṣṭhāna') is a matter on which texts differ and is moved to the uncertainty note.

names.uncertain: The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.

samasa.vigraha: परा देवता परदेवता
samasa.vigraha_iast: parā devatā paradevatā
samasa.explanation: The adjective parā 'supreme' qualifies devatā 'deity' and, in a karmadhāraya, takes its masculine stem para- (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

names.meaning: She who is the supreme Deity
names.significance: She is the deity beyond all deities, Parāśakti, from whom the gods receive their power.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'parAshakti' removed from the meaning; it is the sense, given under significance.

names.meaning: She who is Madhyamā, the middle level of speech
names.significance: Madhyamā is inner speech, where words are formed in sequence in the mind but not yet spoken; traditionally it is placed at the heart.

meaning_check.note: 'stays in the middle' missed the term: in this sequence madhyamā is the third level of speech.

names.uncertain: The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.

samasa.vigraha: वैखरी रूपम् यस्याः सा वैखरीरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: vaikharī rūpam yasyāḥ sā vaikharīrūpā
samasa.explanation: vaikharī and rūpa are co-referential and the whole describes Her: 'She whose form is vaikharī'.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of Vaikharī, audible speech
names.significance: Vaikharī is speech articulated through throat and mouth and heard by the ear: the fourth and outermost level. Every spoken word is thus Her form.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS removed; the parenthesis tidied.

samasa.vigraha: भक्तानाम् मानसम् भक्तमानसम्; भक्तमानसे हंसिका भक्तमानसहंसिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhaktānām mānasam bhaktamānasam; bhaktamānase haṃsikā bhaktamānasahaṃsikā
samasa.explanation: (1) bhakta-mānasa 'the mind of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) haṃsikā 'swan' is the head and the mind stands to it in the locative: 'the swan in the devotees' minds'. mānasa also means Lake Mānasa, home of the swans, so the compound carries a double image.

components.note: haṃsī with the suffix -ka; the ī is shortened before it

names.meaning: She who is the swan in the minds of Her devotees
names.significance: As swans live on Lake Mānasa, She lives in the devotee's mind (mānasa); the swan, said to separate milk from water, is also the emblem of discrimination and of the paramahaṃsa. Compare name 816, munimānasahaṃsikā.
names.previous_split_issues: mānasa was glossed 'mind/lake' without the pun being explained; haṃsikā is a female swan (haṃsī + ka).

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: कामस्य ईश्वरः कामेश्वरः; प्राणस्य नाडी प्राणनाडी; कामेश्वरस्य प्राणनाडी कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmasya īśvaraḥ kāmeśvaraḥ; prāṇasya nāḍī prāṇanāḍī; kāmeśvarasya prāṇanāḍī kāmeśvaraprāṇanāḍī
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-īśvara 'the Lord of desire', Śiva as Kāmeśvara (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) prāṇa-nāḍī 'the channel of the life-breath', the vital artery (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The life-channel is the head and Kāmeśvara stands to it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the very life-channel of Kāmeśvara, Her consort
names.significance: Without Her, Śiva cannot even stir (Saundaryalaharī 1). The Saundaryalaharī (28) also says that the gods who drank nectar perish at the dissolution while Śiva, who drank poison, lives, because of the power of Her earrings: She is His life.

meaning_check.note: nāḍī 'channel, artery' was not translated; ITRANS 'kAmeshvara' removed.

names.previous_split_issues: kāmeśvara was one row; it is kāma + īśvara, joined by guṇa.

samasa.vigraha: कृतम् जानाति इति कृतज्ञा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṛtam jānāti iti kṛtajñā
samasa.explanation: jñā is an agent form of √jñā 'to know' (suffix ka, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), used only after its object: 'she who knows what has been done'. Feminine -ā.

components.meaning: what has been done, a deed; a service done

components.note: √jñā 'to know' with the suffix ka, feminine

names.meaning: She who knows all that is done, and is grateful for it
names.significance: Traditionally She is the inner witness who knows every act as it occurs; in ordinary usage kṛtajña means 'grateful', and She remembers and rewards the least service done to Her.

meaning_check.note: 'as they occur' is interpretive; the ordinary sense of kṛtajña, 'grateful', is added.

names.uncertain: kṛtajñā means both 'knowing what is done' and 'grateful'; both are given.

samasa.vigraha: कामेन पूजिता कामपूजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmena pūjitā kāmapūjitā
samasa.explanation: pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and Kāma stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Kāma
names.significance: Kāma is counted traditionally among the great worshippers of Śrīvidyā, and the kādi form of the fifteen-syllabled mantra is associated with him. Traditionally the name also alludes to Kāmagiri (Kāmarūpa), first of the four pīṭhas that names 375–379 recall.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kAma' removed.

names.uncertain: The allusion to the Kāmagiri pīṭha (reading 'worshipped at Kāma[giri]') is traditional but not in the grammar of the name.

samasa.vigraha: शृङ्गारः एव रसः शृङ्गाररसः; शृङ्गाररसेन सम्पूर्णा शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा
samasa.vigraha_iast: śṛṅgāraḥ eva rasaḥ śṛṅgārarasaḥ; śṛṅgārarasena sampūrṇā śṛṅgārarasasampūrṇā
samasa.explanation: (1) śṛṅgāra-rasa 'the rasa that is śṛṅgāra', the sentiment of love (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The participle sampūrṇā 'completely filled' is the head and the rasa stands to it in the instrumental.

components.meaning: śṛṅgāra, the erotic or romantic sentiment, love

names.meaning: She who is filled with śṛṅgāra, the rasa of love
names.significance: Śṛṅgāra is the first and chief of the rasas of poetics; She is its fullness, the love between Śiva and Śakti. Traditionally the word sampūrṇā also alludes to Pūrṇagiri, the second of the four pīṭhas.

meaning_check.note: 'essence of Love' made precise: śṛṅgāra is the rasa (sentiment) of love.

names.previous_split_issues: The first member had been garbled by a zero-width joiner (śa‍ṛṅgāra); it is śṛṅgāra.

names.meaning: She who is victorious
names.significance: Jayā is also a name of Durgā; She is victory itself, and victory in any field is Hers.

meaning_check.note: 'always and everywhere' is not in the name.

samasa.vigraha: जालन्धरे स्थिता जालन्धरस्थिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: jālandhare sthitā jālandharasthitā
samasa.explanation: The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head and Jālandhara stands to it in the locative of place.

components.meaning: Jālandhara, one of the four principal pīṭhas (seats of the Goddess)

names.meaning: She who abides in the Jālandhara pīṭha
names.significance: Jālandhara is the third of the four pīṭhas (Kāmagiri, Pūrṇagiri, Jālandhara, Oḍyāṇa); in the body it is traditionally placed at the throat (viśuddhi).

meaning_check.note: ITRANS removed; the bodily placement moved to significance.

samasa.vigraha: ओड्याणम् एव पीठम् ओड्याणपीठम्; ओड्याणपीठम् निलयः यस्याः सा ओड्याणपीठनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: oḍyāṇam eva pīṭham oḍyāṇapīṭham; oḍyāṇapīṭham nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā oḍyāṇapīṭhanilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) oḍyāṇa-pīṭha 'the seat that is Oḍyāṇa' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose abode (nilaya) is the Oḍyāṇa seat'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: Oḍyāṇa, one of the four pīṭhas

names.meaning: She whose abode is the Oḍyāṇa pīṭha
names.significance: Oḍyāṇa is the fourth of the four pīṭhas; in the body it is traditionally placed between the eyebrows (ājñā). Beyond the four lies the bindu, the next name.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS removed and 'center' named as pīṭha; the bodily placement moved to significance.

samasa.vigraha: बिन्दुः एव मण्डलम् बिन्दुमण्डलम्; बिन्दुमण्डले वसति इति बिन्दुमण्डलवासिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: binduḥ eva maṇḍalam bindumaṇḍalam; bindumaṇḍale vasati iti bindumaṇḍalavāsinī
samasa.explanation: (1) bindu-maṇḍala 'the circle that is the bindu' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) vāsinī 'dwelling', an agent noun from √vas with ṇini, is compounded with its place in the locative sense.

components.meaning: point; the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra

names.meaning: She who resides in the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra
names.significance: The bindu is the innermost enclosure of the Śrīcakra, the sarvānandamaya cakra, where She is one with Kāmeśvara; in the body it corresponds to the crown, beyond the four pīṭhas.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'bindumaNDala', 'shrI chakra' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: रहसि यागः रहोयागः; रहोयागस्य क्रमः रहोयागक्रमः; रहोयागक्रमेण आराध्या रहोयागक्रमाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: rahasi yāgaḥ rahoyāgaḥ; rahoyāgasya kramaḥ rahoyāgakramaḥ; rahoyāgakrameṇa ārādhyā rahoyāgakramārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) rahas-yāga 'worship in secret' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …yāga-krama 'the ordered method of that worship' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and the method stands to it in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped by the method of secret worship'.

names.meaning: She who is to be worshipped by the method of secret, inner worship
names.significance: Traditionally rahoyāga is antar-yāga, the inner worship in which the offerings are mental and kuṇḍalinī is led through the cakras to unite with Śiva; it is guarded and taught only from teacher to disciple.

meaning_check.note: krama 'method' was not translated and yāga is worship, not specifically 'sacrificial rites'; ārādhyā is 'to be worshipped'.

names.previous_split_issues: raho was given in its sandhi form (the stem is rahas), and kramārādhyā was one row glossed 'worshipped by the method of'; it is krama 'method' + ārādhyā 'to be worshipped'.

sandhi.rule: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66) and visarga before a voiceless sound (8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), which becomes s before t (8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ): the s reappears

samasa.vigraha: रहसि तर्पणम् रहस्तर्पणम्; रहस्तर्पणेन तर्पिता रहस्तर्पणतर्पिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: rahasi tarpaṇam rahastarpaṇam; rahastarpaṇena tarpitā rahastarpaṇatarpitā
samasa.explanation: (1) rahas-tarpaṇa 'a secret oblation' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The participle tarpitā 'gratified' is the head and the oblation stands to it in the instrumental as the means. The same root √tṛp 'to satisfy' gives both members.

names.meaning: She who is gratified by secret offerings of libation
names.significance: Traditionally the secret tarpaṇa is inward: the nectar released when kuṇḍalinī reaches the crown floods and satisfies the deities of the body, or the senses' objects are offered into the fire of consciousness.

meaning_check.note: tarpitā is a past participle, 'gratified', not 'to be gratified'; tarpaṇa is a libation, not 'rites of worship' in general.

sandhi.rule: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66) and then visarga before the voiceless p (8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सद्यः प्रसीदति इति सद्यःप्रसादिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadyaḥ prasīdati iti sadyaḥprasādinī
samasa.explanation: prasādinī is an agent noun from pra + √sad 'to be pleased, gracious' with the suffix ṇini (Pāṇini 3.2.78), which here marks a habit; the indeclinable sadyas 'at once' is compounded with it: 'she who is gracious at once'.

names.meaning: She who bestows Her grace immediately
names.significance: Traditionally She is quickly pleased by sincere devotion, without long austerities; Her grace is not delayed.

samasa.vigraha: विश्वस्य साक्षिणी विश्वसाक्षिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvasya sākṣiṇī viśvasākṣiṇī
samasa.explanation: sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head and the universe stands to it in the genitive.

components.note: sākṣin, from sākṣāt 'with one's own eyes' + -in (Pāṇini 5.2.91 sākṣād draṣṭari saṃjñāyām), feminine

names.meaning: She who is witness to the whole universe
names.significance: As pure consciousness She sees all without being touched by what She sees, as the Upaniṣads describe the Self as the witness (sākṣin).

samasa.vigraha: साक्षिभिः वर्जिता साक्षिवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sākṣibhiḥ varjitā sākṣivarjitā
samasa.explanation: The participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and sākṣin 'witness' stands to it in the instrumental (sākṣin loses its n in composition).

components.note: appears as sākṣi- in the compound

names.meaning: She who has no other witness
names.significance: She is the witness of all, and nothing stands outside Her to witness Her; consciousness is known by itself alone.
names.previous_split_issues: sākṣi was given in its compound form; the stem is sākṣin.

sandhi.rule: the final ṣ of ṣaṣ 'six' becomes ḍ at the end of a member (jaśtva, Pāṇini 8.2.39)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: षट् अङ्गानि षडङ्गानि; षडङ्गानाम् देवताः षडङ्गदेवताः; षडङ्गदेवताभिः युक्ता षडङ्गदेवतायुक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: ṣaṭ aṅgāni ṣaḍaṅgāni; ṣaḍaṅgānām devatāḥ ṣaḍaṅgadevatāḥ; ṣaḍaṅgadevatābhiḥ yuktā ṣaḍaṅgadevatāyuktā
samasa.explanation: (1) ṣaṭ-aṅga 'the six limbs' (a numeral compound, dvigu). (2) …aṅga-devatā 'the deities of the six limbs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The participle yuktā 'accompanied' is the head and the deities stand to it in the instrumental.

components.note: appears as ṣaḍ- in the compound

components.meaning: limb; the 'limbs' of a mantra in nyāsa

names.meaning: She who is accompanied by the deities of the six aṅgas (heart, head, crest, armor, eyes and weapon)
names.significance: In ritual the six limbs of the mantra are placed on the body (aṅga-nyāsa) as heart, head, crest of hair, armor, eyes and weapon. Traditionally the name is also read of Śiva's six attributes: omniscience, contentment, beginningless knowledge, independence, unfailing power and infinite power.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'angAs' removed and the six aṅgas given in their ritual order (hṛdaya, śiras, śikhā, kavaca, netra, astra).

names.previous_split_issues: ṣaḍaṅga was one row; it is ṣaṣ 'six' (as ṣaḍ-) + aṅga 'limb'.

samasa.vigraha: षाड्गुण्येन परिपूरिता षाड्गुण्यपरिपूरिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: ṣāḍguṇyena paripūritā ṣāḍguṇyaparipūritā
samasa.explanation: The participle paripūritā 'completely filled' is the head and ṣāḍguṇya 'the six excellences' stands to it in the instrumental. ṣāḍguṇya is a single derived word (from ṣaḍ-guṇa 'six qualities' with a collective suffix and vṛddhi), so no junction inside it is analysed here.

components.note: ṣaḍguṇa 'six qualities' + the collective suffix -ya with vṛddhi
pari + √pṝ 'to fill', causative, past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is completely filled with the six excellences (bhaga)
names.significance: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa names the six that make up bhaga, divine excellence: complete sovereignty, dharma, glory, fortune, knowledge and dispassion; some lists have valor (vīrya) in place of dharma.

meaning_check.note: The previous list ('prosperity, valor, dispassion, fame, wealth and wisdom') blurred the traditional six; they are named in the significance.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (supsupā, with an adverbial first member)
samasa.vigraha: नित्यम् क्लिन्ना नित्यक्लिन्ना
samasa.vigraha_iast: nityam klinnā nityaklinnā
samasa.explanation: The adverb nityam 'always' qualifies the participle klinnā 'moist': 'ever-moist'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who is ever moist with compassion
names.significance: The moistness is the melting of Her heart in compassion. Nityaklinnā is also the third of the Nityā goddesses of the lunar fortnight (see name 391).

meaning_check.note: The image of moistness (klinnā) is kept rather than reduced to 'compassionate'.

sandhi.rule: the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound

samasa.vigraha: निर्गता उपमा यस्याः सा निरुपमा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirgatā upamā yasyāḥ sā nirupamā
samasa.explanation: nis stands for nirgata 'gone out', and the compound describes Her: 'She from whom all comparison has gone', i.e. who has no equal.

names.meaning: She who is incomparable
names.significance: Nothing can be compared with Her, since there is nothing other than Her; as the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad says, 'there is no likeness of Him' (na tasya pratimā asti).

sandhi.rule: the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound; the r then turns the n of vāna into ṇ (ṇatva)

samasa.vigraha: निर्वाणम् एव सुखम् निर्वाणसुखम्; निर्वाणसुखम् ददाति इति निर्वाणसुखदायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirvāṇam eva sukham nirvāṇasukham; nirvāṇasukham dadāti iti nirvāṇasukhadāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) nirvāṇa-sukha 'the bliss that is liberation' (karmadhāraya of identification; a genitive reading 'the bliss of liberation' gives the same sense). (2) dāyinī 'giver', an agent noun from √dā with ṇini (the root takes y before -in), is compounded with its object.

names.meaning: She who confers the bliss of liberation
names.significance: Nirvāṇa is the 'blowing out' of bondage; its bliss is not a pleasure that ends but the Self's own nature, which She reveals.
names.previous_split_issues: nirvāṇa sukha had been printed as two words and given as one row; it is one compound, nirvāṇa + sukha + dāyinī.

samasa.vigraha: नित्यानाम् षोडशिका नित्याषोडशिका; नित्याषोडशिका रूपम् यस्याः सा नित्याषोडशिकारूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nityānām ṣoḍaśikā nityāṣoḍaśikā; nityāṣoḍaśikā rūpam yasyāḥ sā nityāṣoḍaśikārūpā
samasa.explanation: (1) nityā-ṣoḍaśikā 'the group of sixteen Nityās' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The first member keeps its feminine -ā (nityā, not nitya-) as the name of the goddesses. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the sixteen Nityās'.

components.meaning: Nityā, 'the eternal one', the name of the lunar-day goddesses

names.meaning: She who has the form of the sixteen Nityā goddesses
names.significance: The Nityās are the deities of the lunar days: Kāmeśvarī, Bhagamālinī, Nityaklinnā, Bheruṇḍā, Vahnivāsinī, Mahāvajreśvarī, Śivadūtī, Tvaritā, Kulasundarī, Nityā, Nīlapatākā, Vijayā, Sarvamaṅgalā, Jvālāmālinī and Citrā, with Lalitā Herself as the sixteenth, Mahānityā. Their worship is set out in the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava.

meaning_check.note: The list of the Nityās moves from the meaning to the significance and is put into IAST (Nīlapatākā).

names.previous_split_issues: ṣoḍaśikā was glossed 'sixteen'; it is the collective 'group of sixteen'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: श्रीः कण्ठे यस्य सः श्रीकण्ठः; श्रीकण्ठस्य अर्धम् श्रीकण्ठार्धम्; श्रीकण्ठार्धम् शरीरम् अस्याः अस्ति इति श्रीकण्ठार्धशरीरिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrīḥ kaṇṭhe yasya saḥ śrīkaṇṭhaḥ; śrīkaṇṭhasya ardham śrīkaṇṭhārdham; śrīkaṇṭhārdham śarīram asyāḥ asti iti śrīkaṇṭhārdhaśarīriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) śrī-kaṇṭha 'he in whose throat is beauty' (bahuvrīhi), a name of Śiva, whose throat is marked by the poison He held there. (2) śrīkaṇṭha-ardha 'half of Śrīkaṇṭha' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) This is compounded with śarīra 'body', and the possessive suffix -in makes śarīriṇī: 'She who has half of Śiva as Her body'.

components.meaning: throat; with śrī, Śrīkaṇṭha, a name of Śiva

names.meaning: She who possesses half of the body of Śrīkaṇṭha (Śiva), as Ardhanārīśvara
names.significance: She is the left half of Śiva in the form Ardhanārīśvara, half woman and half man: Śiva and Śakti are inseparable.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shrIkaNTha', 'ardhanArishvara' put into IAST; the two sentences joined.

names.previous_split_issues: śrī was glossed 'sacred/auspicious' as a separate word, and kaṇṭhārdha 'half of Śiva's body'; śrīkaṇṭha is one name of Śiva (śrī + kaṇṭha 'throat'), and ardha 'half' joins it.
names.uncertain: For an exact half Pāṇini's rule (2.2.2 ardhaṃ napuṃsakam) puts ardha first; here, as often in later usage, it follows in a genitive compound.

names.meaning: She who is effulgent
names.significance: Traditionally Her radiance is the light of the deities who surround Her in the Śrīcakra, rays of Her own splendor.

samasa.vigraha: प्रभा रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रभारूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: prabhā rūpam yasyāḥ sā prabhārūpā
samasa.explanation: prabhā 'radiance' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is radiance'.

names.meaning: She who is effulgence
names.significance: She does not merely possess light (previous name); She is light, the light of consciousness by which all else is seen.

names.meaning: She who is celebrated
names.significance: Traditionally She is known to everyone, since She is the 'I' that each being knows as itself, even when Her true nature is not recognized.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: परमा ईश्वरी परमेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: paramā īśvarī parameśvarī
samasa.explanation: The adjective paramā 'supreme' qualifies īśvarī 'sovereign' and takes its masculine stem parama- in the karmadhāraya (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

names.meaning: She who is the supreme sovereign
names.significance: She rules over all rulers, including the gods who govern creation, preservation and dissolution.

samasa.vigraha: मूलम् प्रकृतिः मूलप्रकृतिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: mūlam prakṛtiḥ mūlaprakṛtiḥ
samasa.explanation: mūla 'root' stands in apposition to prakṛti 'nature', the head: 'the Nature that is the root'. prakṛti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

names.meaning: She who is the root Nature (mūlaprakṛti), the first cause of the universe
names.significance: Mūlaprakṛti is the Sāṅkhya term for primal matter, itself uncaused (the Sāṅkhyakārikā: mūlaprakṛtir avikṛtiḥ); in Śrīvidyā this root of all evolution is Her own power.

meaning_check.note: The term mūlaprakṛti is named; 'entire' dropped.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with akta (√añj)

samasa.vigraha: न व्यक्ता अव्यक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: na vyaktā avyaktā
samasa.explanation: The negative na, reduced to a- (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), is compounded with the participle vyaktā 'manifest': 'not manifest'.

components.note: vi + √añj 'to make clear', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is unmanifested
names.significance: Avyakta is the unmanifest state of prakṛti, beyond the great principle (mahat), as the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says: mahataḥ param avyaktam.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: व्यक्तम् च अव्यक्तम् च व्यक्ताव्यक्ते; व्यक्ताव्यक्ते स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vyaktam ca avyaktam ca vyaktāvyakte; vyaktāvyakte svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) vyakta-avyakta 'the manifest and the unmanifest' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) This is compounded with svarūpa 'own nature', and the possessive suffix -in makes svarūpiṇī 'having as Her own nature'.

components.note: sva + rūpa + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

names.meaning: She who is in the manifested and unmanifested forms
names.significance: Both the evolved world and its unevolved cause are Her; She is not only the root (397–398) but also all that grows from it.
names.previous_split_issues: The last member had been misspelled svarūpīṇi; it is svarūpiṇī (short i, long final ī).

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with āpinī

names.meaning: She who is all-pervading
names.significance: There is no place where She is not; as space pervades all pots, She pervades all beings.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: विविधाः आकाराः यस्याः सा विविधाकारा
samasa.vigraha_iast: vividhāḥ ākārāḥ yasyāḥ sā vividhākārā
samasa.explanation: vividha 'various' qualifies ākāra 'form', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose forms are manifold'; ākāra takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who has a multitude of forms
names.significance: Every form in the universe is one of Her forms; traditionally, in worship She takes whatever form the devotee holds dear.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the absorbed a

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: विद्या च अविद्या च विद्याविद्ये; विद्याविद्ये स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vidyā ca avidyā ca vidyāvidye; vidyāvidye svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vidyā'vidyāsvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) vidyā-avidyā 'knowledge and ignorance' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) This is compounded with svarūpa 'own nature', and the possessive suffix -in makes svarūpiṇī.

components.note: sva + rūpa + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

names.meaning: She who is the form of both knowledge and ignorance
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 1) calls Her the supreme knowledge that is the cause of liberation and also the cause of the bondage of saṃsāra; the Īśa Upaniṣad teaches that one crosses death by avidyā and gains immortality by vidyā.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member (over inner karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: कामस्य ईशः कामेशः; महान् कामेशः महाकामेशः; महाकामेशस्य नयने महाकामेशनयने; महाकामेशनयने एव कुमुदे महाकामेशनयनकुमुदे; महाकामेशनयनकुमुदयोः आह्लादः महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादः; महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकारिणी कौमुदी महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकौमुदी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmasya īśaḥ kāmeśaḥ; mahān kāmeśaḥ mahākāmeśaḥ; mahākāmeśasya nayane mahākāmeśanayane; mahākāmeśanayane eva kumude mahākāmeśanayanakumude; mahākāmeśanayanakumudayoḥ āhlādaḥ mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādaḥ; mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādakāriṇī kaumudī mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādakaumudī
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-īśa 'the Lord of desire' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), and mahā-kāmeśa 'the great Kāmeśa' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā-). (2) …kāmeśa-nayana 'the eyes of Mahākāmeśa' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …nayana-kumuda 'the eyes, which are night-lilies' (karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (4) …kumuda-āhlāda 'the gladdening of those lilies' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) …āhlāda-kaumudī 'the moonlight that causes that gladdening' (karmadhāraya with the middle word kāriṇī 'causing' understood). kaumudī is feminine already.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya

components.meaning: the night-blooming white water-lily, which opens to the moon

components.note: from kumuda: the light that delights the night-lilies

names.meaning: She who is the moonlight that gladdens the water-lilies that are Mahākāmeśa's eyes
names.significance: The kumuda opens only at moonrise: Śiva's eyes open in joy only at the sight of Her. Traditionally the image also says that without Her, Śiva does not act.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'whois' and ITRANS 'mahAkAmesha' corrected.

names.previous_split_issues: kumudāhlāda was one row; it is kumuda 'night-lily' + āhlāda 'gladdening'. kāmeśa (kāma + īśa) was glossed only as Śiva.

sandhi.rule: final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o
jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)
m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member (over inner karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: हार्दम् तमः हार्दतमः; भक्तानाम् हार्दतमः भक्तहार्दतमः; भक्तहार्दतमसः भेदः भक्तहार्दतमोभेदः; भानुमतः भानवः भानुमद्भानवः; भानुमद्भानूनाम् सन्ततिः भानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः; भक्तहार्दतमोभेदकारिणी भानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः भक्तहार्दतमोभेदभानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: hārdam tamaḥ hārdatamaḥ; bhaktānām hārdatamaḥ bhaktahārdatamaḥ; bhaktahārdatamasaḥ bhedaḥ bhaktahārdatamobhedaḥ; bhānumataḥ bhānavaḥ bhānumadbhānavaḥ; bhānumadbhānūnām santatiḥ bhānumadbhānusantatiḥ; bhaktahārdatamobhedakāriṇī bhānumadbhānusantatiḥ bhaktahārdatamobhedabhānumadbhānusantatiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) hārda-tamas 'the darkness of the heart' (karmadhāraya; hārda 'belonging to the heart'), and bhakta-hārdatamas 'the heart-darkness of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …tamo-bheda 'the piercing of that darkness' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) bhānumad-bhānu 'the rays of the sun' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; bhānumat 'possessing rays' is the sun) and …bhānu-santati 'a stream of those rays'. (4) The two halves join as a karmadhāraya with 'causing' understood: 'the stream of sunrays that pierces the darkness in the devotees' hearts'. santati is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

names.meaning: She who is the stream of sunrays that dispels the darkness in the hearts of Her devotees
names.significance: A single ray does not end the night; a continuous stream of sunlight does. So Her grace, flowing without break, removes the ignorance in the devotee's heart.

meaning_check.note: 'sunbeam' was singular; santati is a continuous stream of the sun's rays.

names.previous_split_issues: tamo and bhānumad were given in their sandhi forms (stems tamas, bhānumat); bheda is 'piercing', and hārda is the adjective 'of the heart'.

samasa.vigraha: शिवः दूतः यस्याः सा शिवदूती; अथवा शिवस्य दूती शिवदूती
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivaḥ dūtaḥ yasyāḥ sā śivadūtī; athavā śivasya dūtī śivadūtī
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose messenger is Śiva'; the final takes the feminine -ī. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, dūtī 'female messenger' is the head: 'Śiva's messenger'.

names.meaning: She for whom Śiva is the messenger
names.significance: In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 8) the Śakti that emerges from the Goddess sends Śiva Himself as Her envoy to the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha, and so is known as Śivadūtī. Śivadūtī is also the seventh of the Nityā goddesses.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS removed; the second reading ('Śiva's messenger') is given in the samāsa note.

names.uncertain: The bahuvrīhi ('whose messenger is Śiva', as in the Devī Māhātmya story) and the ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('messenger of Śiva') are both current.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शिवेन आराध्या शिवाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivena ārādhyā śivārādhyā
samasa.explanation: ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' (gerundive) is the head and Śiva stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Śiva
names.significance: Even Śiva worships Her: the power by which He is what He is.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' removed.

samasa.vigraha: शिवः मूर्तिः यस्याः सा शिवमूर्तिः; अथवा शिवा मूर्तिः शिवमूर्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivaḥ mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā śivamūrtiḥ; athavā śivā mūrtiḥ śivamūrtiḥ
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi, Śiva and mūrti 'form' are co-referential: 'She whose form is Śiva'. As a karmadhāraya, śivā 'auspicious' qualifies mūrti: 'the auspicious form'. mūrti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

names.meaning: She whose form is Śiva Himself
names.significance: Śiva and Śakti are one; Her form is His. Read the other way, Her form is auspiciousness itself.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' removed.

names.uncertain: 'whose form is Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'auspicious form' (karmadhāraya) are both possible.

sandhi.rule: m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra becomes ṅ before k (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शिवम् करोति इति शिवङ्करी
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivam karoti iti śivaṅkarī
samasa.explanation: karī is an agent form of √kṛ 'to make', compounded with its object śiva 'auspiciousness, welfare': 'she who brings about welfare'. The m before kara is the augment mum, as in bhayaṅkara, kṣemaṅkara (Pāṇini 6.3.67 arurdviṣadajantasya mum); it may also be taken as the accusative ending kept. Either way the surface is śivaṅ-.

components.note: √kṛ 'to do' with an agent suffix, feminine

names.meaning: She who brings about auspiciousness
names.significance: Traditionally also: She makes Her devotees into Śiva, bringing them to identity with Him.

meaning_check.note: The second reading ('turns Her devotees into Śiva') is traditional and moves to significance; ITRANS removed.

samasa.vigraha: शिवस्य प्रिया शिवप्रिया; अथवा शिवः प्रियः यस्याः सा शिवप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivasya priyā śivapriyā; athavā śivaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā śivapriyā
samasa.explanation: As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, priyā 'beloved' is the head: 'the beloved of Śiva'. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom Śiva is dear'. Both are true of Her.

names.meaning: She who is beloved of Śiva
names.significance: She is dear to Śiva and Śiva is dear to Her; the love of the divine couple is the model of the devotee's love.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' removed.

samasa.vigraha: शिवः परः यस्याः सा शिवपरा; अथवा शिवात् परा शिवपरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivaḥ paraḥ yasyāḥ sā śivaparā; athavā śivāt parā śivaparā
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi, para 'highest, devoted to' is predicated of Śiva: 'She for whom Śiva is the highest', i.e. wholly devoted to Him. As a pañcamī-tatpuruṣa: 'She who is beyond Śiva'.

names.meaning: She who is solely devoted to Śiva
names.significance: She has no aim but Śiva; read the other way, She is beyond even Śiva, as the supreme power.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' removed.

names.previous_split_issues: parā was glossed 'supreme' only; here it is 'wholly devoted to' (or 'beyond').
names.uncertain: 'devoted to Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'beyond Śiva' (pañcamī-tatpuruṣa) are both current; the meaning follows the first.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शिष्टानाम् इष्टा शिष्टेष्टा; अथवा शिष्टैः इष्टा शिष्टेष्टा
samasa.vigraha_iast: śiṣṭānām iṣṭā śiṣṭeṣṭā; athavā śiṣṭaiḥ iṣṭā śiṣṭeṣṭā
samasa.explanation: iṣṭā is the head. From √iṣ 'to desire' it means 'dear, desired', and the righteous stand to it in the genitive: 'dear to the righteous'. From √yaj 'to worship' it means 'worshipped', and they stand to it in the instrumental: 'worshipped by the righteous'.

components.meaning: the disciplined, the cultured; those who follow the Veda

components.note: √iṣ 'to desire' or √yaj 'to worship', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is dear to the righteous
names.significance: She is the chosen deity (iṣṭa-devatā) of the disciplined, who worship Her; traditionally She in turn loves those who live by dharma.

meaning_check.note: Three alternative glosses reduced to one; the others are given under significance and uncertainty.

names.uncertain: iṣṭā may be from √iṣ ('dear to the righteous') or √yaj ('worshipped by the righteous'); a bahuvrīhi 'to whom the righteous are dear' is also given by some.

samasa.vigraha: शिष्टैः पूजिता शिष्टपूजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: śiṣṭaiḥ pūjitā śiṣṭapūjitā
samasa.explanation: pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and the śiṣṭas stand to it in the instrumental as the agents.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by the righteous
names.significance: The śiṣṭas, those trained in the Veda and its discipline, are traditionally the standard of right practice; their worship of Her is itself authority for Her worship.

meaning_check.note: 'always' is not in the name.

samasa.vigraha: न प्रमेया अप्रमेया
samasa.vigraha_iast: na prameyā aprameyā
samasa.explanation: The negative na, reduced to a- (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), is compounded with the gerundive prameyā 'to be measured, known by a means of knowledge'.

names.meaning: She who is immeasurable, beyond every means of knowledge
names.significance: No means of valid knowledge (pramāṇa), perception, inference or any other, can make Her its object, since She is the consciousness by which they all work.

meaning_check.note: 'by the senses' was too narrow: prameya is what any pramāṇa can measure.

samasa.vigraha: स्वः प्रकाशः यस्याः सा स्वप्रकाशा
samasa.vigraha_iast: svaḥ prakāśaḥ yasyāḥ sā svaprakāśā
samasa.explanation: sva 'own' qualifies prakāśa 'light', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose light is Her own'. A tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa reading ('shining by Herself', svena prakāśā) gives the same sense.

names.meaning: She who is self-luminous
names.significance: 'Everything shines after Him as He shines; by His light all this is lit' (tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam, Kaṭha and Muṇḍaka Upaniṣads). She needs no other light to be known.

sandhi.rule: final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o

samasa.type: a genitive dvandva governed by a nañ-tatpuruṣa, written as one name
samasa.vigraha: मनांसि च वाचः च मनोवाचः; न गोचरा अगोचरा; मनोवाचाम् अगोचरा मनोवाचामगोचरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: manāṃsi ca vācaḥ ca manovācaḥ; na gocarā agocarā; manovācām agocarā manovācāmagocarā
samasa.explanation: (1) mano-vāc 'minds and words' (itaretara-dvandva), here in the genitive plural, manovācām. (2) a-gocarā 'not within the range' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; gocara 'range of the senses', used adjectivally and made feminine). (3) The genitive depends on agocarā: 'not within the range of minds and words'. The genitive ending is kept, so this is either a compound that retains its case ending (aluk) or two words read together as one name; the m of vācām simply stands before the a of agocarā.

names.meaning: She who is beyond the range of mind and speech
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the bliss of Brahman: 'from which words turn back, together with the mind, not having reached it' (yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha).
names.previous_split_issues: The split read vācāma + gocarā; it is vācām 'of words' (genitive plural) + agocarā 'beyond the range of'.
names.uncertain: Whether manovācām agocarā is one compound with the genitive retained or two words read as a single name is not settled; the meaning is the same.

sandhi.rule: t becomes c before ś (Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ), and ś after it becomes ch (8.4.63 śaś cho 'ṭi, optional): cit + śakti → cicchakti

samasa.vigraha: चित् एव शक्तिः चिच्छक्तिः; अथवा चितः शक्तिः चिच्छक्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: cit eva śaktiḥ cicchaktiḥ; athavā citaḥ śaktiḥ cicchaktiḥ
samasa.explanation: As a karmadhāraya: 'the power that is consciousness'. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the power of consciousness'. śakti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

names.meaning: She who is the power of consciousness
names.significance: Names 416–419 pair Her sentient and insentient powers: consciousness (416–417) and the inert world (418–419); both are one Śakti.
names.previous_split_issues: cic and chaktiḥ were given in their sandhi forms; the members are cit 'consciousness' and śakti 'power'.

samasa.vigraha: चेतना रूपम् यस्याः सा चेतनारूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: cetanā rūpam yasyāḥ sā cetanārūpā
samasa.explanation: cetanā 'sentience' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is sentience'.

names.meaning: She whose form is awareness (cetanā)
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5) salutes the Goddess 'who in all beings is called awareness' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu cetanety abhidhīyate): the sentience by which each being knows.

meaning_check.note: 'pure' is not in the name; cetanā is awareness as it animates beings.

samasa.vigraha: जडा शक्तिः जडशक्तिः; अथवा जडस्य शक्तिः जडशक्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: jaḍā śaktiḥ jaḍaśaktiḥ; athavā jaḍasya śaktiḥ jaḍaśaktiḥ
samasa.explanation: As a karmadhāraya: 'the insentient power' (jaḍā takes the stem jaḍa- by puṃvadbhāva). As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the power of (that which is) insentient', i.e. the power that becomes matter.

names.meaning: She who is the power that becomes the insentient world
names.significance: Traditionally this is māyā, Her power as the material cause, which transforms itself into the inert universe; it complements cicchakti (416).

meaning_check.note: The previous gloss ('the māyā that has transformed itself as the power of creation') gave commentary as translation; the name says 'the power of the insentient'. The māyā reading moves to significance.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: जडः आत्मा यस्याः सा जडात्मिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: jaḍaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā jaḍātmikā
samasa.explanation: jaḍa 'insentient' and ātman 'self, nature' are co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose nature is the insentient'. The bahuvrīhi takes the suffix kap (ātman → ātmaka), and the feminine is -ikā (Pāṇini 7.3.44).

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the inanimate world
names.significance: The inert world too is Her, as the sentient beings are; nothing is outside Her.

names.meaning: She who is the Gāyatrī mantra
names.significance: The Gāyatrī (tat savitur vareṇyam, Ṛgveda 3.62.10) is the mother of the Vedas; the traditional derivation explains the name as that which protects the one who sings it (gāyantaṃ trāyate). Names 420–423 recall the twilight worship (sandhyā-vandana) of the twice-born.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'gAyatrI' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with āhṛti

components.meaning: utterance; the sacred utterances bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ

names.meaning: She who is the Vyāhṛti, the sacred utterance
names.significance: The vyāhṛtis bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ are uttered before the Gāyatrī; they name the three worlds. Traditionally She is also all utterance, the power of speech.

meaning_check.note: The technical sense, the vyāhṛtis that precede the Gāyatrī, is named; 'presides over the power of speech' moves to significance.

sandhi.rule: m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

components.meaning: twilight, the junction of day and night; the twilight worship

names.meaning: She who is in the form of twilight
names.significance: Sandhyā is the junction of night and day and the worship performed at those junctions; She is both the hour and the rite.
names.uncertain: The word is derived from sam + √dhyai ('meditation') or from sandhi 'junction' (sam + √dhā); both are traditional.

sandhi.rule: ṣatva: the s of √sev becomes ṣ after the prefix ni

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an upapada-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: द्विः जातः द्विजः; द्विजानाम् वृन्दम् द्विजवृन्दम्; द्विजवृन्देन निषेविता द्विजवृन्दनिषेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: dviḥ jātaḥ dvijaḥ; dvijānām vṛndam dvijavṛndam; dvijavṛndena niṣevitā dvijavṛndaniṣevitā
samasa.explanation: (1) dvi-ja 'twice-born' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; ja from √jan 'to be born'). (2) dvija-vṛnda 'the host of the twice-born' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The participle niṣevitā 'served, worshipped' is the head and the host stands to it in the instrumental.

components.meaning: twice-born; one initiated into the Veda

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by hosts of the twice-born
names.significance: The twice-born worship Her daily through the Gāyatrī at the twilights; the second birth is initiation into the Veda.

meaning_check.note: vṛnda 'host, multitude' was not translated.

verse_notes.note: The four levels of speech run through this śloka: parā (366), paśyantī (368), madhyamā (370) and vaikharī (371), interleaved with 367 and 369. Name 367 pratyak-citī: the k is the c of pratyac before c-.
Names 375–379 are traditionally read as recalling the four pīṭhas: Kāma(giri) in 375, Pūrṇa(giri) in 376 sampūrṇā, then Jālandhara (378) and Oḍyāṇa (379); the bindu (380) lies beyond them.
381 raho-yāga: raho is rahas before a voiced sound; 382 keeps the s (rahas-tarpaṇa) before t.
383 keeps the visarga inside the name: sadyaḥ-prasādinī.

Nityaklinnā (388), Śivadūtī (405) and Vijayā (346) are also names of individual Nityā goddesses; 391 names the sixteen together. 390 is one compound (nirvāṇa-sukha-dāyinī), though it was printed as two words.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga after i becomes r before a vowel (the r of ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66)

verse_notes.note: mūlaprakṛtiḥ (397) and avyaktā (398) are separate names; the r of -prakṛtir is the visarga before a-.

The half-line in text.json reads विद्याविद्या-स्वरूपिणी, with a hyphen typed into the Devanagari and without the avagraha that the name (402) has; see the text concern on 402. Name 403 fills the whole second half.
Name 404 fills the first half. Names 405–410 (into śloka 89) all begin with śiva-; 408 śivaṅkarī is śivam + karī.
Name 415 divides mano-vācām + agocarā ('beyond the range of minds and words'), not vācāma + gocarā.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes s before a voiceless stop (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ), and that s becomes ś before the palatal c (8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ)
visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound (the r of ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66)

verse_notes.note: Names 416–419 pair the sentient and insentient powers; 420–423 recall the twilight worship (Gāyatrī, vyāhṛti, sandhyā, the twice-born). The visarga of vyāhṛtiḥ stands unchanged before s- (optional, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari).

report.summary: Checked all 58 names of ślokas 81–90 against text.json: sandhi at every member and visible prefix junction (including the visarga and anusvāra forms of rahas-, sadyas-, tamas-, śivam-), layered samāsa analyses with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Most changes are ITRANS and wording tidying; two meanings were replaced (367 pratyakcitīrūpā, where pratyak is 'inward', not 'unmanifested'; 418 jaḍaśaktiḥ, where commentary had been given as translation). One word boundary was wrong in the old split (415: manovācām agocarā, not vācāma gocarā). The Sanskrit wording is sound; one orthographic concern is recorded: the half-line of śloka 87 has a stray hyphen and lacks the avagraha of name 402.

text_concerns.concern: Not an error of wording: text.json writes this name with an avagraha (विद्याऽविद्या…), but the half-line of śloka 87 has विद्याविद्या-स्वरूपिणी, without the avagraha and with a hyphen typed into the Devanagari. The half-line should probably read विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी (or both without ऽ), with no hyphen, as the edition's correction of name 391 did for नित्या-षोडशिका.
